assignments.reason: Coast and Djeffara from Gabes through the Emporia, Tripolitania and Leptis to the Altars of the Philaeni
Magas' Cyrenaica: the Pentapolis, the Jebel Akhdar plateau and the east Syrtis shore, from the Altars of the Philaeni to the Catabathmus

Ptolemaic Marmarica from the Catabathmus (Paraetonium station) to Alexandria, and the Western Desert edge and oases up to the Nile (north part: Marmarica coast and the Nile edge, held even where desert)

Oasis belt of the Western Desert (Bahariya, Farafra, Kharga side) south of 29.8N: only what lies within reach of a town or the Nile stays Egyptian; the empty deep desert between stays unowned (lead decision)
Mauri country between the Atlantic and the Muluya, Rif to Sous, was left with unowned holes in the Atlas and the Moulouya corridor
The Atlantic coast south of the Sous to Cape Juby is one Mauretanian band; its inland fringe was left unowned beside owned coast
Masaesyli country east of the Muluya, Oranie and Hautes Plaines; a Mauretanian patch sat inside it
Gaetuli steppe south of the Atlas, Draa to Figuig to the Saharan Atlas, as one belt instead of scattered patches
Southern Tunisia (Nefzaoua, Djerid), the Lesser Syrtis and the Emporia hinterland south of the Carthaginian block, to the Tripolitanian interior
Great Syrtis coast west of the Altars of the Philaeni (18.3E)
Great Syrtis coast east of the Altars of the Philaeni, the Cyrenaican border
Cyrenaican coast and plateau east to the Catabathmus (25.15E), where Egypt begins
Draa and Anti-Atlas edge below the Gaetuli belt (the grey pocket near -5E, 29N; not the Tarfaya coast, which is already Mauretanian)
The Nile valley and the desert within about 100 km of it, both banks: Delta hinterland, Wadi Natrun, Fayum, Middle Egypt to Qena (lead decision)

notes: Applied in order, later wins; a province is decided by its centre. Checked against the 253 settlements: no polygon changes the owner of a province that holds a settlement whose controller is fixed (Carthage, Hadrumetum, Thapsus/Leptis Minor, Utica/Hippo Diarrhytus, Hippo Regius stay Carthage; Iol and Cirta stay Numidian; Tingis, Volubilis stay Mauretanian; Cyrene, Apollonia stay Cyrene; Garama stays Garamantes).

Reading of the id cyrene: the kingdom of Magas (governor c. 300-276, self-styled king 276-250, half-brother of Ptolemy II, allied by marriage with Antiochus I). In 270 it is an independent monarchy at war with, or in armed truce against, Egypt, NOT a Ptolemaic province. Ptolemy III recovers it by marriage (Berenice II) after 250. It already has a monarchy government form in the scenario.

DECISION FOR THE LEAD (Gaetuli): the gaetuli-pre-saharan-belt assignment turns 113 provinces (87 unowned, 26 Mauretanian) into one Gaetuli belt. It cuts against the rule that open desert is held by no one. Alternative: delete that assignment and instead assign the 12 old Gaetuli patches to unowned (leave the Mauretanian edge as is). The belt is my recommendation because the game map names these regions gaetulia, tafilalt and draa, and Strabo/Pliny put the Gaetuli exactly there, but the tribes were nomads and no state can be dated.

LOW CONFIDENCE, not applied: Carthaginian posts on the Atlantic (Lixus, Mogador, Kerne) and the Punic coast of Algeria (Rusicade, Chullu, Saldae, Icosium, Siga). Hanno colonies were largely lapsed by 270. Tingis is fixed Mauretanian by the scenario.

LOW CONFIDENCE, not applied: the Carthage/Numidia frontier in eastern Algeria and western Tunisia (Hippo Regius to Sicca to Capsa). The current diagonal border from (6.0E,36.9N) to (9.4E,34.9N) is smooth and defensible; the Fossa Regia (146 BCE) and Massinissa gains are later. The coast strip west of Hippo Regius to about 6.0E (Rusicade, Chullu) is Carthaginian on the current map, plausible for the Punic emporia.

LOW CONFIDENCE, not applied: the Syrtic interior (Nasamones around Augila, Marmaridae inland from the Catabathmus) is left unowned; only the coast and plateau go to Carthage, Cyrene, Egypt. Siwa (25.5E, 29.2N) and Augila lie outside the province set.

The Fezzan/Garamantes is one province at Garama (13.0E, 26.5N); the map has no provinces around it, so nothing to correct. The Canary Islands (10 provinces) are correct as canarian-peoples (Guanche-ancestor peoples, untouched by Carthage).

Egypt west edge: 25.15E is the Catabathmus (Sollum), the boundary Magas reached and Egypt held; Paraetonium is Ptolemaic. The Western Desert assignment to lon 28.6E-30.6E, lat 26.4N up gives Egypt the oasis belt (Bahariya, Farafra, Kharga side), consistent with docs/egypt-arabia-270-bce.md, but it overrides the open-desert rule as well: drop the lower rectangle (south of 29.8N) if the lead wants desert unowned.

Massyli/Masaesyli split: not implemented; see docs/north-africa-270-bce.md for the recommendation. If it is ever made, the Masaesyli/Massyli line is drawn at about 5.0E on the coast, following the Numidia/Titteri region break (Masaesyli west including Iol, Siga and the Hodna; Massyli east including Cirta, Nementcha and Aures).
